**The failing test.** The EUR19 case was rejected correctly. Only the message was wrong: it said "text is absent" and never mentioned the numeric boundary. `verifyPageExpectation` now reports the missing text and the offending values separately. Rejection is unchanged.

**The five review items**
1. **Source URLs.** Unsupported, missing and unknown records now carry `candidateSources` (id, url, kind) as a structured field. Only supported records have `snippet` and `sourceUrl`, taken from the actual page text. Unsupported values never get a snippet.
2. **No silent truncation.** `toArtifactEvidence` keeps every record and throws "Too many numeric values" above `EVIDENCE_RECORD_BUDGET` (2000). A single text with more than 200 distinct numbers is also rejected. Only the tool-result reports (`evidenceReport`) are capped, and they set `recordsTruncated`.
3. **Completion summary.**
   - The report's `summary` is now always `groundedSummary(task)`, built from recorded state.
   - The model's text goes in a separate `modelSummary` field. It is `{status:"withheld"}` with no text if any number in it lacks page, file or recorded-code evidence.
   - Operational counts no longer count as evidence, so "2 features" is withheld even when `calls == 2`. The test covers this.
4. **`acknowledgeUnsupportedNumbers`.** The saved note text gets an `[UNVERIFIED NUMERIC VALUES - NOT SUPPORTED BY ATTACHED SOURCE EVIDENCE: …]` line, and the artifact metadata keeps `acknowledgedUnknown` plus the `unknown` records. A recheck gives `fullySupported:false`, so `verify.artifact` returns `verified:false`. Without the flag, unsupported values are rejected before anything is written. The same rejection applies at `write_sheet`, `write_gtm`, `verify_sheet`, `verify_gtm`, `verify.artifact` and the completion validator.
5. **Limitations.**
   - Checking is lexical: each number, price or currency amount is tokenised and matched to the observed text of the attached source with boundaries (19 is not 199 or 19.5, `$19` is not EUR19, 19% is not 19, 9k is not 9, `$ 19` equals `$19`, `19.00` equals `19`).
   - Non-numeric claims are not proven ("fastest", "supports SSO"). Only the existing exact-excerpt GTM check and human review cover them.
   - The match does not tie a number to its product or plan. A note saying "Beta is $19" passes if `$19` appears anywhere in that note's declared source, even when it belongs to a different plan.
   - Numbers written as words ("nineteen", "twenty dollars") are not extracted, so they are not checked.
   - A bare claimed `19` can match `$19` or `19 users` on the page.
   - `$` and USD are treated as different currencies.
   - Source text is capped at 18,000 characters, so numbers past that are unsupported.
   - Rechecks use the current observation map. If a page is re-observed with different text, earlier support is dropped.
   - GTM launch and email drafts must also carry only page-visible numbers, so Piccolo's own numbers get rejected there.
   - Notes that cite image sources can only pass with the acknowledge flag.

Spelled-out amounts and explicit free-price phrases are now checked like digits. `npm test` passes 67 of 67 (64 before, 3 new tests) and `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. I did not launch the app or run any scripts, and `ADAL_USAGE.md` is untouched.

**What changed**
- **Number words:**
  - Covered words are zero to nineteen, the tens, hundred, thousand, million, billion and trillion.
  - Hyphenated or spaced compounds ("twenty-one", "one hundred and five") are read as one phrase.
  - A trailing dollars, euros, pounds, cents or percent is part of the phrase.
  - Phrases are lowercased, with hyphens turned into spaces and the currency word made plural, then compared exactly.
- **Free-price phrases:** "free forever", "forever free", "free for life", "free of charge", "at no cost", "at no charge", "no cost" and "no charge" must appear in full in the attached observed source. A page saying only "Free" does not support "Free forever". "No cost" is supported by "at no cost", because the page states it.
- **Word boundaries:** letters on either side of a word stop the match, so "ElevenLabs" and "Someone" produce no number tokens.
- **Where it applies:** the extractor is shared, so notes, sheet cells, GTM excerpts and free text, the `verify.page` retry pins and the completion-summary audit all pick this up. Missing support gets the same records as digits: supported records carry a real snippet and source URL, and unsupported ones carry candidate sources and no snippet. Notes can still use the acknowledge flag to keep an unproven phrase marked unknown. The completion report's own summary is still built from recorded steps.
- **Digits:** digit and currency behavior is unchanged, and all earlier tests still pass.

**New tests** (all in `tests/agent-evidence.test.ts`)
1. Absent "twenty dollars" and absent "free forever" are flagged. Supported word phrases return real snippets. Digits and words don't cross-support, and "twenty euros" doesn't match "twenty dollars".
2. "ElevenLabs" and "Someone" are not tokenized as number words, while "eleven dollars" is.
3. Spelled-out amounts are flagged in notes, sheet cells and acknowledged notes. A `verify.page` retry that changes or drops a spelled-out amount is rejected.

**Changed files:** `src/shared/agent-evidence.ts` and `tests/agent-evidence.test.ts`.

**Limitations**
- Support is exact phrase matching only. "Twenty dollars" is not supported by `$20`, "20 dollars" or "twenty bucks", and "one hundred" is not supported by "one hundred and five".
- "One" is included as a number word, so prose like "no one" or "one of" also needs source support or an "unknown" rewrite. This is deliberately strict.
- The word list stops at trillion, so words like "dozen", "half", "couple", "several" and ordinals ("twentieth") are not checked.
- Only the eight listed free phrases are detected. "Free", "free tier", "free plan", "100% free" and "costs nothing" are not.
- Number-to-product association and non-numeric semantic claims are still not proven, so this is not a fact checker.
